name: Astronomy
boundaries: Astronomy: fundamental discoveries and enabling technologies within this field. Include cross-field consequences where the central advance belongs to this field; exclude routine incremental optimization. Use the historical breakthroughs in the prompt to calibrate revolutionary impact.

original_dispositions.reason: A confirmed distant giant planet would be a major Solar System discovery, but its existence, mass and proposed orbital effects are uncertain. Discovery alone would add one object to a known class and would not necessarily establish the claimed formation history. On the calibration used here, the assured conceptual advance falls below the threshold. The historical mass and distance ranges are hypotheses, not established facts.
Atmospheric disequilibrium is a possible line of evidence, not an automatic proof.
The entry is framed as a quantitative physical energy budget, allowing multiple mechanisms and distinguishing that result from downstream forecasting.
A strict redshift greater than 15–20 is not made a defining criterion; the decisive issue is reliable identification of a metal-free first-generation source or its distinctive immediate products.
Direct detection is distinguished from existing indirect cosmological evidence.

original_dispositions.original_title: Unified origin of all fast radio bursts
original_dispositions.reason: Solving the emission mechanisms would be important, but the assumption that all bursts share one origin is unsupported, and a complete classification alone is not clearly comparable to the list’s foundational threshold. Moreover, a Galactic magnetar has already produced an FRB-like event. FRBs can be useful cosmological probes without first being established as standard candles.

Not added as a separate concept. A resolution caused by calibration or analysis systematics would be consequential but would not necessarily reveal new physical law. A verified new cause of acceleration is covered by AST-04; other genuinely new physics revealed by a resolution would need its own evidence and assessment. No arbitrary “below one sigma” criterion is imposed.
The result need not demonstrate an extant civilization or impose any particular policy response.

The broad late-universe budget has progressed beyond the historical list’s characterization of roughly half of normal matter as simply unobserved. A 2026 analysis reports evidence for diffuse warm-hot gas and infers a substantial baryon fraction there, with broad uncertainty and model dependencies; it is not a complete spatial map of every baryon. A more precise census would be valuable, but the remaining increment is not specified here as a separate revolutionary capability.
The revised concept allows multiple channels and requires evidence separating birth conditions from subsequent growth.
